chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from al-Hasan ibn Musa al-Khashshab from Ghiyath ibn Kalub from Isḥaq ibn 'Ammar from Ja'far from his father (peace be upon them both) that 'Ali (peace be upon him) used to say:

"Stepdaughters are forbidden to you alongside the mothers with whom you have consummated the marriage; they are equal whether in the household or not. And the mothers are ambiguous: whether you have consummated the marriage with the daughters or not, so forbid [them] and make ambiguous what God has made ambiguous."

key_terms.الرَّبَائِبُ: Stepdaughters (daughters of one's wife from another man)
key_terms.الْمُبْهَمَاتُ: Ambiguous/uncertain (referring to the status of the prohibition)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on marrying stepdaughters in Shia jurisprudence according to Imam Ali?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) narrates from Imam Ali (peace be upon him) that stepdaughters are forbidden if the marriage with their mother is consummated, extending the prohibition to all stepdaughters regardless of cohabitation or consummation with the daughter. This ruling employs the principle of 'ibhām' (divine ambiguity), where the Prophet was instructed to prohibit what God left ambiguous, thereby establishing a comprehensive barrier of affinity. This hadith highlights the Shia emphasis on the practical application of Quranic ambiguity in deriving detailed familial prohibitions.
